views.name: Orders due in the next 7 days

cells.text: Order quantity minus good units from finished runs, never below zero
Plan another run if it is above zero when the previous run is done
Scrapped units divided by good plus scrapped units
Over 5 percent means look at the material or the jig before the next run
Reorder level minus on hand, never below zero
Add it to the next purchase and check the lead time against the due dates

text.text: Every order follows the same path. Each handoff has one owner and one thing that must be true before it passes on.

cells.text: Must be true to move on
Customer has price, date and finish in writing
Deposit received and parts checked against the recipe
At least one run planned for every unit
Final inspection passed and carrier booked

text.text: Walk the Orders due in the next 7 days list with the supervisor and decide what to overtime, move or tell the customer about.
Quality is built in at each step, not added at the end. Three checks per run catch most problems early.
First article: measure the first piece before the batch continues.
In process: check joints and dimensions halfway through.
Final inspection: look at every unit before packing.
Stop the run and write what was found on the check row.
Rework only with the supervisor's approval; record rework as such.
If the cause is material or tooling, add a note to the part or product.
Running out of a part stops the whole line. A weekly stock walk keeps the reorder list honest.
Count on-hand for parts marked Low
Update the On hand figure on each row
Check lead times against orders due in the next three weeks
Reorder level = average weekly use times lead time in weeks, plus a safety margin you can explain. Review it each quarter.
